reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the general concept that heterogeneous microstructures in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA can improve strength-ductility synergy via back-stress mechanisms, but neither passage describes cryo-rolling, warm-rolling, or the specific 800°C/1h annealing, nor do they provide quantitative support for the claimed improvements in modulus and fracture resistance.
premises: Cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling and annealing creates a heterogeneous nanostructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1
Heterogeneous microstructure generates strain gradients and GNDs producing long-range back-stresses
Back-stresses delay necking and crack initiation while promoting work-hardening
The hybrid process yields ~15-20% higher strength and ~10% higher ductility than standard processing
The hybrid process improves Young's modulus and fracture resistance
